players: 8-10 (numbers below are for 8; '+1/+2' says what to add)
theme: Breaking a mid-block: overload the last line and switch
focus: In possession against a mid-block: drop the 8 on an angle, switch through the 6 in one action to find the far-side 2v1, and create a central 3v2 on their CBs
objectives: Get one more attacker than they have defenders on their last line (5v4 in the full team, 3v2 or 4v3 in today's units)
6 receives on the open side and switches in one action (back foot to front foot) to find the 2v1 on the far side
8, 9 and W create a central 3v2 on their 2 CBs and play the pass through the lines
key_messages: "Plus one" - one more on their back line than they have
"Open up, switch" - receive on the back foot, play off the front foot
"Make them shuffle" - move the ball until the far side opens
"Three on two" - 8, 9 and W against their centre-backs

blocks.title: Switch rondo: two boxes and a 6

diagram.caption: 3v1 in one end box; after 4 passes, play into the 6, who switches to the far box in one action. The presser sprints across.

blocks.setup: One 40x15m area split into 3 boxes (14m / 12m / 14m). 8 players: 3 in each end box, a 6 in the middle, 1 presser. 9: add a second presser (3v2). 10: add a second 6.
how: 3v1 (or 3v2) in the start box: after 4 passes, play into the 6.
6 receives on the open side and switches to the far box in one action (receive left, play right).
Presser sprints across to the far box; repeat.
Presser wins it: swaps with the player who lost it. Change the 6 every 2 minutes.
blocks.link_to_theme: Warms up the 6's back-foot-to-front-foot switch and the idea that the far side opens when they shuffle.
coaching_points: 6 opens their body before receiving - shoulders already facing the far box
First touch sets the ball onto the stick for the switch, not a stop then a turn
End-box players make the angle for the 6 so the pass to them isn't straight through the presser
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone is in the area; presser changes on every turnover so nobody presses for more than about a minute.

blocks.title: Drop, switch, 2v1

diagram.caption: Full pitch width. 8 drops on an angle, ball goes 8 to 6, 6 opens up and switches to the far side for the RB + RW 2v1 on their FB.

blocks.setup: 40m long, full width (55m). 8 players: blue CB, 8, 6, RB, RW v red 2 forwards + FB. Blue score by dribbling through the blue gate on the far side. 9: add a red midfielder who guards the 6. 10: add a blue LW high on the near side and a red second FB.
how: Walk through at 50%: 8 drops on an angle beside the CB (not all the way to full-back) and receives facing forward.
Their 2 forwards shuffle across. Ball goes 8 to 6 (if the forward steps to the 8, play back to the CB, who drops off for a new angle).
6 receives on the open side behind their 2 forwards and switches to the RB in one action.
RB and RW play the 2v1 against their FB and dribble through the gate.
Then 75%, then live. Rotate 3 players into red every 4 minutes; last 6 minutes switch to the other side.
blocks.link_to_theme: The key moves from the video against a mid-block: the dropped 8, the CB question, and the switch through the 6.
coaching_points: 8 drops at an angle so they face forward on receiving - an open body sees both the far side and the 6
6 positions behind and between their 2 forwards, ready to receive left and play right in one action
Make them shuffle first: 2-3 passes on one side, then switch - don't switch too early
Far-side RB and RW stay wide and high so the 2v1 is ready when the ball arrives
questions: Their forward followed our 6: who is free?
When is the right moment to switch?
progressions: Red can press when the ball goes backwards
regressions: Remove the red FB (RB and RW go 2v0 - just time the switch)
blocks.activity_notes: All 8-10 involved every rep; reps reset from the CB every 15-20 seconds.

blocks.title: Central 3v2 to goal

diagram.caption: 8 opens out to the FB, then plays the reverse pass through the lines to the W. 8, 9 and W against 2 CBs = central 3v2.

blocks.setup: 45x40m, 2 mini goals on the end line. 8 players: blue 5 (6, 8, LB, LW, 9) v red 3 (2 CBs + FB). Red counter by dribbling over the start line. 9: add a red midfielder (5v4). 10: add a blue RW and a red second FB (6v5, the full 5v4 on their back line).
how: Coach feeds the 6 or the 8 in the build zone.
Goal = 1. Goal from a central 3v2 (8, 9 and W all in the middle against their 2 CBs) = 2.
Red win it: dribble over the start line = 1.
Swap 3 players into red every 4 minutes.
blocks.link_to_theme: Uses the overload on their last line and the central 3v2 to finish, the end product of the whole block.
coaching_points: 8: open out to the FB, then look inside for the reverse pass on the W's back foot
W receives between their FB and CB, and if they can't turn, plays back to the 8 and the ball moves on
9 pins both CBs; the 8 arrives late as the third attacker
If the near side is crowded, play back to the 6 and go again
regressions: Red FB can't leave the wide lane
Red CBs can't tackle, only intercept
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone plays; coach keeps a ball-stock at the start line for instant restarts.

step.space: Narrow to 32m to make the 3v2 harder to find
step.task: Bonus only counts if the 6 touched the ball in the move

blocks.title: 4v4 (+ floaters): beat the block

diagram.caption: 4v4 with end zones. Out of possession, teams can't press in the opponent's end zone. Switch of play into a goal = 2.

blocks.setup: 50x40m with 12m end zones, 2 mini goals at each end. 8 players: 4v4. 9: 1 neutral floater who plays as the 6 for the team in possession. 10: 5v5.
how: Restarts always from the team's CB in their end zone.
Out of possession, you can't press in the opponent's end zone, so you have to hold a block.
Goal = 1. Goal that came after a switch of play = 2. Goal from a central 3v2 = 3.
4 x 4-minute games, 1 minute rest. Last game: remove the no-press zones.
blocks.link_to_theme: Rehearses the whole plan against a team holding a block, the way a mid-block opponent will on a Saturday.
coaching_points: Patience: circulate until their block shuffles, then switch
CB drops off to give their forward a question: follow or protect the centre?
Weeks 1-3 still apply - lanes, rotation chain, someone moves, I move
progressions: Defending team can press anywhere (the 'Saturday press')
regressions: Floater plays even at 8 (rotate the role)
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone plays; ball-stocks behind both ends.

blocks.title: 4v4 / 5v5 on the half pitch: the whole picture
blocks.setup: Half pitch, full goal at one end (GK if one trains, otherwise 2 mini goals), 2 mini goals on halfway. 4v4, 4v4+1 or 5v5. Swap ends at 10 minutes.
how: Normal game - no conditions.
Focus: all four principles from the block.
Coach tallies: completed rotations, switches of play, goals from an overload.
coaching_points: Plus one on their last line, then switch
questions: Which principle gave us the most chances this month? Which one do we still need?

safety: Shin guards and gum shields for all
Switches are flat slaps or hits along the ground - no raised balls
If a GK trains, they must be fully kitted before going in goal
reflection_prompts: Could the 6 switch in one action, or did they need a stop-turn-play?
Did we get plus one on their last line? Who was missing?
What do we revisit in the next block?
